title: Causal Graph and Effect Identification from Pooled Count Data with Known Compositions
banked_reason: D0.5 terminal kernel_substituted@oeq:three-node-benchmark: the accepted focal Xi0/Xi1 proof-producing certificate remains open, while only conditional certifier and existence machinery was delivered.
gap_reasons: The proposal's concrete early-kill deliverable was a certified grid with positive global margins and useful precision, but the core delivers only an existence theorem and conditional certifier while the sole prescribed benchmark remains open.
Neither prescribed run of \(\mathfrak C\) has a supplied validated proof object.

proof_attempt_summary: Discovery proved the unrestricted full-column-rank recovery frontier, a positive-Poisson converse, stability, causal transfer, finite-grid existence, and soundness of a conditional tri-valued certifier. The accepted focal contribution nevertheless required executing that certifier on Xi0 and, if needed, Xi1 with a complete outward-rounded proof object; no such executable bounded implementation or certificate was produced. D0.5 therefore rejected the conditional framework as a substitute for the promised concrete kernel.
tldr: Known linearly independent raw-count compositions recover unrestricted labeled type laws for arbitrary \(p\geq1\) by a logarithmic count-PGF inverse, with positive Poisson aliases proving necessity. For \(p\geq2\), any recovered count-valued law in the published causally minimal, pairwise-identifiable CPCM class then has its labeled DAG identified; the three-coordinate condition is not part of graph recovery. Intervention contrasts and validation use the stricter compact positive-polynomial Poisson subclass. For \(p\geq3\), the headline is a finite sound tri-valued certifier: it always terminates, and only a \(\mathtt{CERTIFIED}\) output verifies a rational chart-projection cover together with wrong-graph separation, global within-graph injectivity, local Jacobian nonsingularity, interiority, PGF-tail, and designated-contrast precision bounds. The finite-grid theorem separately proves existence of some finite rational grid and cover with positive exact margins; it does not certify either prescribed synthetic input. Pointwise sample-split Wald inference is conditional on certification, the capped certified-design frontier is finite, and the three-node base/conditional-refinement benchmark status remains open.
gap: Transform inversion, direct-law CPCM and Poisson-thinning DAG identification, and validated numerics are established separately, but no result recovers labeled type laws through known multi-composition pools and propagates infinite-support PGF tails through distinct wrong-graph, global within-graph, local-regularity, and causal-precision certificates.
fill: The project combines the arbitrary-dimensional rank frontier with a finite \(p\geq3\) certifier that constructs and verifies a rational chart-projection cover, a deterministic estimator, an arithmetic ceiling, and a finite Pareto design class.
